# DDD Knowledge Freshness Mandate

## Rule

YOU MUST keep `.ai/harness/ddd-ubiquitous-language.md` and `.ai/harness/ddd-project.md`
current. These files are the domain knowledge backbone. Stale domain knowledge causes
INCORRECT code generation, wrong variable names, and domain model violations.

## Before Starting ANY Work [MANDATORY — NO EXCEPTIONS]

> **Ordering (no-tool-before-gate):** these reads are a context-load step, not a
> pre-gate action. If your agent defines a startup gate (preflight / first-token /
> no-tool-before-gate), do them as the FIRST step INSIDE that gate, never before it;
> if it has no such gate, do them first. The reads stay MANDATORY — only their
> ordering relative to your own gate changes (see the root files' Operating Contract).

1. READ `.ai/harness/ddd-project.md` first (per Ordering above) — this is your onboarding document.
   It contains: project identity, tech stack, folder structure, important files,
   known gotchas, authoritative sources, and source debt. Without this, you operate blind.
2. READ `.ai/harness/ddd-ubiquitous-language.md` — load domain vocabulary.
   Every domain term has a code artifact mapping. Use ONLY these terms.
3. USE domain terms consistently in ALL code, comments, variable names, and communication.
4. If a file references domain concepts → RE-READ the ubiquitous language section for that concept.

**WHY THIS IS NON-NEGOTIABLE**: These two files provide the contextual understanding
that transforms generic code generation into domain-aware, production-correct output.
An agent that skips these files will use wrong terminology, violate domain invariants,
and produce code that looks correct but is semantically wrong.

## During Work

1. If you discover a NEW domain concept → ADD it to ubiquitous language immediately
2. If you discover a domain term is WRONG → CORRECT it immediately
3. If project structure CHANGES → UPDATE ddd-project.md immediately
4. If you find a new GOTCHA → ADD to ddd-project.md "Known Gotchas" section

## Before Ending Work

1. VERIFY ubiquitous language entries match current code
2. VERIFY project structure in ddd-project.md matches filesystem
3. VERIFY authoritative source catalog entries still match local versions,
   config, and source applicability; unresolved source drift becomes Source Debt
4. UPDATE "Last Updated" section in both files

## Non-Negotiable

- NEVER use domain terms not in the ubiquitous language
- NEVER skip reading DDD files before domain-touching changes
- NEVER leave stale entries — update or mark as deprecated
- Stale DDD files = domain model corruption = code generation failures
- These files are MORE IMPORTANT than rules — rules constrain behavior,
  DDD files constrain UNDERSTANDING
